metadata.title: 2016 Case 17
metadata.original_presentation: A 60-year-old woman was seen in the outpatient pulmonary clinic of this hospital because of increasing dyspnea.

required.content: What is the patient's history of presenting illness?
required.response: The patient had been well until 2 years before the current evaluation, when episodes of mild, nonproductive coughing developed and occurred multiple times daily. Between 13 months and 10 months before the current evaluation, three febrile illnesses occurred, with temperatures up to 38.9°C. After the third illness, the patient noted dyspnea with exertion.

teaching_points.content: Chronic cough and recurrent febrile illnesses can be indicative of underlying pulmonary pathology.

required.content: What treatments were administered during the patient's previous evaluations?
required.response: Oral azithromycin and combined inhaled budesonide–formoterol fumarate dihydrate were administered. Levofloxacin was administered after a chest radiograph showed pulmonary findings suggestive of possible scarring or consolidation.

teaching_points.content: Antibiotics and inhaled corticosteroids are common treatments for respiratory infections and obstructive lung diseases.

required.content: What are the patient's past medical history and lifestyle factors?
required.response: The patient had hypothyroidism, hypercholesterolemia, hypertensive disorder, recurrent urinary tract infections, and lichen sclerosus. She had smoked one to two packs of cigarettes weekly for 10 years as a young adult.

teaching_points.content: Smoking history is a significant risk factor for chronic lung diseases.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD)
refuting_evidence: no mention of wheezing or significant sputum production

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Interstitial Lung Disease (ILD)
refuting_evidence: no specific mention of crackles on lung exam
additional_information_needed: high-resolution CT scan of the chest

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Pulmonary Fibrosis
refuting_evidence: no specific mention of clubbing or crackles
additional_information_needed: high-resolution CT scan of the chest

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Bronchiectasis
refuting_evidence: no mention of significant sputum production

required.content: What were the findings on physical examination?
required.response: The temperature was 36.7°C, the blood pressure 132/63 mm Hg, the pulse 81 beats per minute, the respiratory rate 16 breaths per minute, and the oxygen saturation 93% while she was breathing ambient air. The lungs were clear, and the remainder of the examination was normal.

teaching_points.content: Normal lung sounds do not rule out underlying pulmonary pathology.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD)
refuting_evidence: oxygen saturation slightly low but not severely impaired
additional_information_needed: spirometry to assess for obstructive pattern
chest CT to evaluate for emphysema or chronic bronchitis

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Interstitial Lung Disease (ILD)
additional_information_needed: high-resolution CT scan of the chest
pulmonary function tests to assess for restrictive pattern

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Asthma
refuting_evidence: no significant improvement with inhaled budesonide–formoterol

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Pulmonary Fibrosis
additional_information_needed: high-resolution CT scan of the chest
lung biopsy if diagnosis remains unclear

required.content: What were the results of the pulmonary function tests?
required.response: Pulmonary-function tests were thought to be consistent with obstructive lung disease. The level of α1-antitrypsin was normal.

teaching_points.content: Pulmonary function tests are crucial in diagnosing and assessing the severity of obstructive lung diseases.

required.content: What did the CT scans reveal?
required.response: CT of the chest revealed mild cylindrical bronchiectasis predominantly in the lower lobes, with mild, diffuse bronchial-wall thickening and a small focus of atelectasis or scarring.

teaching_points.content: Bronchiectasis is characterized by permanent dilation of bronchi and can be associated with chronic infections.

required.content: What were the findings from the bronchoscopy?
required.response: Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid revealed clear and colorless fluid, with no evidence of pepsin A or galactomannan antigen. Cytologic examination revealed no viral cytopathic changes, fungal elements, or malignant cells.

teaching_points.content: Bronchoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage can help diagnose infections and other lung conditions.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD)
supporting_evidence: obstructive lung disease pattern on PFTs
refuting_evidence: lungs were clear on physical examination

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Bronchiectasis
supporting_evidence: CT showing mild cylindrical bronchiectasis and bronchial-wall thickening
additional_information_needed: History of childhood respiratory infections or conditions

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Interstitial Lung Disease
refuting_evidence: CT findings more consistent with bronchiectasis
additional_information_needed: Detailed occupational and environmental exposure history

required.response: Albuterol (by nebulizer or by inhaler with a spacer) and a course of azithromycin were administered.

teaching_points.content: Bronchodilators and antibiotics are commonly used in the management of respiratory conditions.

final_diagnosis.name: Bronchiectasis
key_features: Obstructive lung disease pattern on PFTs
